course_name_original: Sistema para el diseño y desarrollo del producto
prerequisites: Diseño y comunicación de producto y automatización de elementos en planta
All subjects from lower courses must be passed or currently enrolled.

learning_outcomes.text: Know the CAD tools and technologies oriented to product-assembly.
Understand how Product Lifecycle Management is performed in the data structure for the company.
Know the Expert Systems currently available for integrated design and manufacturing.
Acquire skills in handling group-oriented solid modeling systems and parametric design.
Acquire criteria to select appropriate technologies and tools in each case for assisted design, automated manufacturing, product definition, product communication, and reverse engineering.
Acquire concepts and skills for generating drawings and documents from three-dimensional geometries.
Know and practically leverage creativity techniques.

syllabus_topics: Concepts, definitions, and aspects involved in new product development.
The design process. Stages and characteristics.
Phases at macrostructure and microstructure level.
Introduction to creative techniques. Main creative techniques.
Lateral thinking: E. De Bono's techniques.
Technologies involved in the different stages of a product's life (CAx).
Types of Models: Classical, virtual, realistic.
Elaboration of physical prototypes using additive manufacturing techniques.
Concept and characteristics of parametric design.
Introduction to concurrent engineering and intelligent systems in industrial design.
Product design and development in concurrent engineering and distributed engineering environments.
The field of artificial intelligence in design.
Design in the company's organizational chart.
Design management manual in the company.
Management of graphic information and revision control.
Product Lifecycle Management (PLM) Systems. Topologies, standards, and interconnection alternatives.
Standard formats for CAD graphics. ACIS, IGES, STEP, and XML. Limitations and recommendations.
The CIM pyramid in the company. Levels and graphic information flow.
Review of the current panorama in industrial design.
Selection of the industrial product to be developed. Definition of the problem to be solved. Identification of design factors related to its life cycle.
Execution of creative sessions using appropriate techniques. Evaluation and selection of ideas. Determination of their degree of inventiveness and innovation.

Execution of the usual design process, structuring the needs of potential customers, defining the technical requirements of the product, identifying its functions, and carrying out a complete functional analysis together with a Quality Function Deployment (QFD) study.
Elaboration and documentation of the virtual model and the complete definition and manufacturing drawings.
Elaboration of a functional physical prototype.
Performance of conceptual tests based on simulations.
Definition of an intelligent optimization system for all or part of the design process followed.
Documentation and presentation of the developed industrial product.
teaching_methods: Practical sessions with ICT support (project work)
Seminars (reinforcement activities, idea search, theoretical content explanation, analysis and evaluation of proposals, definition of simulation models and intelligent systems)
Tutored work (continuous contact and coordination with professor)

assessment_methods.method: Development questions exam (theoretical and practical content)
Project (design, development, and proof of concept of a new industrial product)
Technical report of practical results (including memory, detailed plans, budget, graphic material, simulation, and programming files)

assessment_rules: The overall grade is calculated based on the weighted average of assessment components. To pass the subject, a minimum of 5.0 points out of 10 is required for the overall grade, and also a minimum of 5.0 points in both theoretical and practical content evaluations. There are two modalities for the first call: continuous assessment and non-continuous (global) assessment. Students who do not pass continuous assessment or opt for global assessment must take a comprehensive final exam and complete a project for the first call. For the second call, evaluation will be solely through a comprehensive global exam, which also requires a project. Any unethical behavior will result in a failing grade of 0.0 for the academic year.
